objective: Build the sparring bot in packages/chess-core: a pure module (src/bot.ts) that, given a FEN, picks the bot's move from real human games when the position has enough explorer games (weighted random sampling by games played), and otherwise asks the engine for a reduced-strength move. Every returned move is legality-checked in code and carries its source ("explorer" or "engine"). Export it from src/index.ts. Then write the terminal demo packages/chess-core/scripts/demo-bot.ts (run by `pnpm demo:bot`) that wires the real WASM Stockfish and the real Lichess explorer client into the bot and plays an opening, printing each move with its source label.
contract:
Requirements (docs/requirements.md):
- FR-1: The player can start a game against the sparring bot as White or Black.
- FR-2: During the opening, the bot picks its moves from real human games at a configurable rating band, sampled in proportion to how often each move is played (Lichess opening explorer).
- FR-3: Once the position is out of the explorer data (too few games below a threshold), the bot switches to Stockfish at a reduced strength set for the player's level.
- FR-10 (spirit, for this module): code decides what is true; never return a move that was not checked legal in the position.

Architecture §3.3:
  if explorer.totalGames >= minGames (config):  sample a move weighted by games played
  else:                                          BotEngine.bestMove(fen, { elo: botElo })

config/tutor.json (current, the caller passes the bot block in; do not read files from src):
  "bot": { "explorerRatings": [1200, 1400], "explorerSpeeds": ["blitz", "rapid"], "minGames": 20, "outOfBookElo": 1400 }

chess-core must not depend on engine/explorer at runtime (src stays pure, no I/O; types.ts already mirrors engine types structurally). Define structural interfaces in chess-core for what the bot needs. The real implementations, verbatim:

@chess-tutor/explorer (packages/explorer/src/types.ts, client.ts):
  export interface ExplorerMove { uci: string; san: string; games: number; white: number; draws: number; black: number; averageRating: number; }
  export type OutOfBookReason = "rate_limited" | "server_error" | "network" | "timeout" | "bad_response";
  export interface ExplorerResult { moves: ExplorerMove[] /* sorted by games desc, top 12 only, so sum(moves.games) can be < totalGames */; totalGames: number; opening: { eco: string; name: string } | null; unavailable?: OutOfBookReason /* then moves [] and totalGames 0 */; }
  export interface LookupOptions { ratings: number[]; speeds: string[]; }
  export interface ExplorerClient { lookup(fen: string, options: LookupOptions): Promise<ExplorerResult>; }
  export class ExplorerConfigError extends Error {}  // thrown by lookup on a 401; a misconfiguration
  export function createExplorerClient(opts: { token: string; cache: ExplorerCache; fetch?; timeoutMs?; failureCooldownMs?; baseUrl? }): ExplorerClient  // throws ExplorerConfigError if token empty
  export function createSqliteExplorerCache(...)  // read packages/explorer/src/cache.ts for its signature

@chess-tutor/engine (packages/engine/src/types.ts, index.ts):
  export interface BestMoveOptions { elo?: number /* UCI_LimitStrength + UCI_Elo */; movetimeMs?: number; depth?: number; }
  export interface Engine { analyze(fen, opts?): Promise<Analysis>; bestMove(fen: string, opts?: BestMoveOptions): Promise<string /* UCI */>; quit(): Promise<void>; }
  export { createEngineFromEnv, createWasmEngine, createNativeEngine } from "./stockfish-engine.ts"  // read it for signatures; createEngineFromEnv uses STOCKFISH_PATH if set, else WASM

Existing chess-core helpers you can reuse (src/moves.ts): playUci(chess, uci) -> chess.js Move (throws on illegal/non-promotion suffix), sanOf(fen, uci), toUci(move). chess.js ^1.4.0 is the only runtime dependency.

Behaviour decisions (coordinator):
1. Sampling: when the result is available and totalGames >= minGames, sample among the listed moves with weight = games (moves with games <= 0 excluded). Moves not listed (beyond top 12) are ignored. Randomness is injected (random: () => number in [0,1), default Math.random) so tests are deterministic.
2. Fallback to engine when: explorer result unavailable; totalGames < minGames; no listed move with games > 0; or the sampled explorer move is illegal in the FEN (drop it and resample among the remaining legal listed moves first; engine only if none remain). An explorer lookup that rejects with a generic error also falls back to the engine. An ExplorerConfigError (match by name === "ExplorerConfigError", since you can't import the class) is rethrown: a misconfiguration must be loud.
3. Engine move: bestMove(fen, { elo: outOfBookElo }). Validate it with playUci; if illegal, throw an Error naming the move and FEN (never return it).
4. Game over (checkmate/stalemate/draw by chess.js) or invalid FEN: throw before calling anything.
5. Return shape (suggested, adjust names if you must and say so): { uci: string; san: string; source: "explorer" | "engine"; explorer?: { games: number; totalGames: number; share: number } ; fallbackReason?: "unavailable" | "few_games" | "no_moves" | "lookup_failed" | "illegal_explorer_move" }.
6. Factory suggested: createSparringBot({ explorer, engine, config: { explorerRatings, explorerSpeeds, minGames, outOfBookElo }, random? }) -> { chooseMove(fen): Promise<BotMove> }. Validate config at construction (minGames >= 1 integer, outOfBookElo positive, ratings/speeds non-empty) and throw on bad config.

Demo (packages/chess-core/scripts/demo-bot.ts), run from the root with `pnpm demo:bot [-- --as white|black] [-- --moves N]`. The scripts are already committed at base 30a1ab7:
  root package.json:   "demo:bot": "pnpm --filter @chess-tutor/chess-core demo:bot"
  chess-core package.json: "demo:bot": "node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings=ExperimentalWarning --env-file-if-exists=../../.env scripts/demo-bot.ts"
  chess-core devDependencies: { "@chess-tutor/engine": "workspace:*", "@chess-tutor/explorer": "workspace:*" } (installed, lockfile committed)
- --as is the human's colour (default white). The human side is scripted: as white, London moves d2d4, c1f4, e2e3, g1f3, c2c3, f1d3, b1d2, e1g1 in order, skipping any that are illegal and then using the engine at full strength (bestMove with no elo); as black, KID moves g8f6, g7g6, f8g7, d7d6, e8g8, e7e5, b8d7, c7c6 the same way. The bot plays the other side.
- --moves N full moves (default 10). Print a numbered move list; each bot move labelled "from explorer (G of T games, P%)" or "from engine (~1400) - <reason>".
- Reads LICHESS_TOKEN from the environment (never prints it). If it is missing, print a clear message saying how to set it and exit 1. Explorer cache: an SQLite file in the OS temp dir or in-memory if the cache API allows. Always quit the engine (finally).
- Read config/tutor.json's bot block at runtime from the script (scripts may do I/O; src may not).
